envelope.text: EMITS THROUGH ITS PARENT (records carry the parent's name and filter at

why:
phase-417 stage 0 — visible only because the rclcpp adapter (then `rclcpp_compat.hpp`; deleted at stage 6 step A, each declaration moved to the header owning its concept) became a translation unit (issue 1020). The shim ships this TYPE as a name, so its members stop inheriting "we do not have this type" and become their own claim. Not a new gap: a gap INSIDE a type we ship is a different statement from one about a type we do not.

phase-467 — the C++ half of the pair `c:log_severity_t` rests on: no `get_child` means no dotted name, which is why that row's missing ancestry walk has no hierarchy to walk and is recorded there as a permanent bound rather than as work. See `rust:Logger::create_child` for the constraint itself.

RFC-0102 (2026-10-05) -- DECIDED, NOT YET BUILT (phase-479). The constraint above no longer holds: `get_or_create_logger` copies runtime names into a static arena, `parent.child` fits a 48-byte stack buffer, and `rclcpp::Logger` owns its name since issue 1682. RFC-0102 adopts `get_child`/`create_child` with rcutils's nearest-ancestor level inheritance held as a parent pointer, and reverses the PERMANENT bound recorded here. This row moves to adopt-bounded when phase-479 W2 lands.

phase-479 (2026-10-05) -- LANDED. `rclcpp::Logger::get_child(const std::string&)` (and a `const char*` overload) returns a Logger named `<this>.<suffix>` whose unset level is its nearest ancestor's, as rcutils resolves it -- upstream's naming AND its inheritance (RFC-0102 D1/D2). Bounded where upstream is not (D3): a child over 48 bytes, or made when the runtime-logger arena is full, is not created; it emits through the parent (records carry the parent's name and level) and `set_level` on it is refused rather than moving the parent's threshold; one warning per process. The catch-all's children are top-level names. `/rosout` publication of children (Iron+'s `add_sublogger`) is decided per ROS release by the `/rosout` sink (D4), not here. Held by `logger_names_and_levels_runtime.cpp` section 7 (`just check cpp`).
